correctness.rationale: For exactly two hyperedges A and B, source size a>=3, overlap 1<=c<min(a,b), target threshold k, all A initially active, all B\A inactive, per-vertex exponential recovery delta, whole-group activation rates alpha and beta, c<k forces P=0. If c>=k, excursions start from all A active; competing clocks yield success S=E beta/(alpha+beta)*(1-exp(-(alpha+beta)T_B)), extinction E=E exp(-alpha T_A-beta T_B), and renewal P=S/(S+E). The r=c-k+1-th overlap death rank J is hypergeometric w_j=binom(j-1,r-1) binom(a-j,c-r)/binom(a,c), independent of exponential spacings with rates (a-i+1)delta. Their Laplace products give the displayed exact finite sums. At fixed a,c,k,beta,delta, S~beta/alpha and E~a!delta^a/alpha^a, so 1-P~a!delta^a/(beta alpha^(a-1)), independent of c,k in leading term. Independently solved exact rational full 2^a microstate harmonic chains for a=3..5 across overlap/threshold examples including c<k; formula agrees. The original concrete case P=720/767 is reproduced.

value.rationale: PASS. In threshold hypergraph contagion, whether a finite infectious source activates a neighboring overlapping group before extinction is a natural first-bridge observable. The hypergeometric death-rank formula collapses a growing absorbing state space to a short explicit finite sum; the leading strong-reinforcement failure term unexpectedly loses all overlap and target-threshold dependence despite finite-alpha dependence. This is a motivated reusable exact benchmark, not an arbitrary one-off calculation.
